frequency_question: How often does a recipient state successfully establish domestic production of complex foreign advanced missiles within a tight window under wartime friction?
membership_rule: Includes: wartime programs for domesticating foreign missile systems. Excludes: standard peacetime licensed defense production, domestic production of unguided munitions, or foreign direct supply without domestic line creation.
window: 2 years (matching the structural duration of the prompt)

cases.name: Ukraine domestic production attempts of Western air defense (e.g., FrankenSAM initiatives, though not cruise missiles)
Ukraine domestic adaptation of Neptune anti-ship missiles under wartime friction
Taiwan attempts at domestic mass-production of complex foreign-designed advanced cruise missiles under external pressure

coverage_note: 3 named cases representing the extremely narrow class of wartime/high-pressure domestic precision missile/weapon integration.
known_gaps: Extremely small class size due to the rarity of high-intensity conventional war involving advanced Western missile transfers.
skeleton: 3 identified programs under high-friction conditions; 2 achieved operational status within compressed timelines.
validity_reason: Rapid technological and supply chain adaptations in modern wartime remain relatively stable in baseline friction levels over multi-year horizons.
